# strong-style

- ID: `MD050`
- Category: Emphasis
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: yes
- Tags: `emphasis`

All bold text uses one marker, \*\*text\*\* or \_\_text\_\_, except \*\* inside
a word.

## Why

One bold marker throughout makes the source easier to read. Underscores do not
mark emphasis inside a word, so \*\* stays allowed there.

## Options

Set them under `rules.strong-style.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `consistent`): Marker of strong emphasis to
  require. consistent takes the marker of the first strong emphasis. Values:
  `consistent`, `asterisk`, `underscore`.

## Fix

The fix swaps the markers. gomdlint reports bold text without a fix when the new
marker could pair with characters around it, as in \*\*snake\_case\*\*. It does
the same inside square brackets that are, or could become, the label of a
reference link. gomdlint may report a finding without a fix when the fix would
change a line with one character in brackets, such as \[x\] or \[1\], or the
lines around it up to a blank line, because it could add or remove a task list
checkbox.

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  strong-style:
    options:
      style: consistent
```

Under `rules`, `strong-style: false` turns the rule off and
`strong-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable strong-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line strong-style -->
```
